name: Cheval Blanc Paris
tagline: Seventy-two rooms and suites in La Samaritaine, facing the Pont Neuf.
description:
Cheval Blanc Paris is a 72-room hotel inside the Art Deco building of La Samaritaine, at 8 quai du Louvre, between the Louvre and Le Marais. It faces the Pont Neuf and the Seine, and holds a Dior spa, a 30-metre pool and five restaurants with six Michelin stars between them.

La Samaritaine was designed by Henri Sauvage in 1928, and the hotel occupies the part of it that looks onto the river. The interiors are by Peter Marino, who planned the house in the spirit of a private apartment, with furniture drawn for it and works by Sonia Delaunay, Vik Muniz and Claude and François-Xavier Lalanne. A horse sculpture by Frank Gehry stands in the hotel, and a woven-metal staircase by Sophie Mallebranche runs from the entrance hall to the spa.

The 72 rooms and suites start with the Deluxe Room at 45 square metres, which has a marble bathroom with a bath and a hammam shower, a dressing room and a desk. Four room types differ by view: the Haussmann rooftops, the Louvre colonnade, a side view of the Seine and the Pont Neuf. The Seine Suite measures 105 square metres, and the Notre-Dame Suite and the Eiffel Suite 100 square metres each, with views of the cathedral towers and the Eiffel Tower. On the eighth and ninth floors the Quintessence Suite covers 650 square metres with four bedrooms, a pool and a terrace, and joined to the Ravel Suite it becomes L'Appartement, a 1,000-square-metre duplex with seven bedrooms and a private entrance and lift.

Plénitude, on the first floor, is the three-Michelin-star restaurant of Arnaud Donckele and Maxime Frédéric. Hakuba is a Japanese restaurant with two stars, open for dinner Tuesday to Saturday. Le Tout-Paris on the seventh floor is a brasserie and cocktail bar with one star and a terrace over the Seine, open every day from 7 am to 1 am. Langosteria serves Italian cooking, and Carte Blanche is the in-room dining.

Dior Spa Cheval Blanc has treatment suites, and guests have the curved infinity pool with its handmade mosaics, a hammam, a sauna and a snow shower. The pool is open from 6:30 am to 10 pm. Le Carrousel is a children's club, and there is a Rossano Ferretti hair salon. A private boat takes guests along the Seine at twilight.

The hotel suits visitors who want the centre of Paris on the doorstep, with the Louvre across the road and the river below the window.
